name: live_coalesce_with_literal_default_is_never_null
description: COALESCE over a nullable column with a literal default is inferred non-nullable; the live engine must never return NULL for it, including for the row whose underlying column is NULL
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE users (id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, email TEXT, created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now())
query_sql:
-- @name ListUserEmailsWithDefault
-- @returns :many
SELECT id, COALESCE(email, 'none@example.com') AS email_or_default FROM users ORDER BY id

columns.name: email_or_default
columns.note: COALESCE with a literal default guarantees non-NULL even where email is NULL

sqlc_comparison.sqlc_behavior: sqlc marks the COALESCE result nullable because its first argument is nullable
sqlc_comparison.scythe_improvement: scythe infers non-nullable from the literal default, and this fixture proves the claim is sound against live engines by seeding a row whose email is NULL -- the case that would expose an unsound non-nullable inference

default: INSERT INTO users (id, name, email) VALUES (1, 'Ada Lovelace', 'ada@example.com')
INSERT INTO users (id, name, email) VALUES (2, 'Grace Hopper', NULL)
